cars.variant: H6C short-chassis Kellner Skiff — 1928 Revs Institute reference
cars.specification_market: Original H6/H6B/H6C production-road family, selected 1928 H6C short-chassis Kellner Skiff at Revs Institute, serial 11739. All eight attributes use that exact collection record. Keep the museum technical header's 194 bhp at 3000 rpm as a quoted reference value without an assumed SAE/DIN test standard or universal factory-stock claim. Retain 3370 lb without an inferred dry/kerb basis and 133-inch wheelbase without applying it to long-chassis H6s. Family servo-assisted four-wheel braking is stated by the custodian; no hydraulic actuation or particular servo drive mechanism inferred. No H6B displacement/output, separate bare-chassis data, racing tune, Tulipwood construction, Dubonnet suspension or modern Carmen specifications are transferred. French programme origin is distinct from the marque's Spanish founding. Group original road bodies, engine versions and years once. Dedicated racers, special chassis, replicas and additional coachwork examples are not separate admissions.
cars.summary: The H6 family is a landmark of high-performance road-car engineering, combining an aviation-derived overhead-camshaft six with servo-assisted four-wheel brakes. The short-chassis H6C Skiff illustrates its sporting application. Count the original H6/H6B/H6C road family once across bodies and years; price, rarity and decorative coachwork alone are not admission reasons.
